title: Minimum Adjacent Swaps to Make Array Alternating Even‑Odd
statement: Given an array `nums` of integers, you may swap any two adjacent elements. Return the minimum number of adjacent swaps required to rearrange the array so that even and odd numbers strictly alternate (i.e., for every index `i`, `parity(nums[i]) != parity(nums[i+1])`). If it is impossible to achieve such an arrangement, return `-1`.
summary: Compute the minimum number of adjacent swaps needed to arrange the array so that even and odd numbers alternate.
constraints: The answer fits in a 64‑bit signed integer.

examples.explanation: All numbers are even; no alternating arrangement exists.
Swap the element at index 1 (value 1) with the element at index 2 (value 2) → [1,2,1,2].
